Dalí used this method to bring forth the hallucinatory forms, double images and visual illusions that filled his paintings during the Thirties.  As with the earlier "Metamorphosis of Narcissus", "Swans Reflecting Elephants" uses the reflection in a lake to create the double image seen in the painting. Here, the three swans in front of bleak, leafless trees are reflected in the lake so that the swans' necks become the elephants' trunks and the trees become the legs of the elephants.
